Converting NumPy arrays to PyTorch tensors
In PyTorch, we use tensors to encode the inputs and outputs of a model, as well as the model’s parameters. Tensors are similar to NumPy’s ndarrays,
except that tensors can run on GPUs or other specialized hardware to accelerate computing
1. Converting NumPy arrays to PyTorch tensors

children.label: 1. Converting NumPy arrays to PyTorch tensors

children.value: A torch.Tensor is a multi-dimensional matrix containing elements of a single data type. Calculations between tensors can only happen if the tensors share the same dtype. In some cases tensors are used as a replacement for NumPy to use the power of GPUs (more on this later). Let's try to initialize a numpy array first!

import torch
import numpy as np
import sys

x = torch.from_numpy(arr)
# Equivalent to x = torch.as_tensor(arr)
print(x)

# Print the tensor object type
print(type(x))
print(x.type()) # this is more specific!

rows, cols = 5, 5

# Create matrix using array comprehension
mat = np.matrix([[np.round(np.random.random(), 3) for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)])
print(mat)
print(type(mat))


xmat = torch.from_numpy(mat)
print(xmat)
print(type(xmat))

# Check if an object is a tensor
torch.is_tensor(mat)

Most arithmetic operations require float values. Those that do work with integers return integer tensors.

is the sum of the products of the corresponding entries of two 1D tensors. If the tensors are both vectors, the dot product is given as:
$\begin{bmatrix} a & b & c \end{bmatrix} \;\cdot\; \begin{bmatrix} d & e & f \end{bmatrix} = ad + be + cf$
If the tensors include a column vector, then the dot product is the sum of the result of the multiplied matrices. For example:
$\begin{bmatrix} a & b & c \end{bmatrix} \;\cdot\; \begin{bmatrix} d \\ e \\ f \end{bmatrix} = ad + be + cf$
Dot products can be expressed as

a = torch.tensor([1,2,3], dtype=torch.float)
b = torch.tensor([4,5,6], dtype=torch.float)
print(a.dot(b))
